sentences.en: Our star-spangled Union Jack flutters so proud over the dancing heads of the merry patriotic crowd.
sentences.zh: 我们那星条旗般的联合杰克旗，在欢快爱国人群的舞动头顶上骄傲地飘扬。

sentences.en: Yeah, tip your hat to the Yankee conquerors.
sentences.zh: 是啊，向那些扬基征服者脱帽致敬吧。

sentences.en: We've got no reds under the bed with guns under our pillows.
sentences.zh: 我们可没在床底下藏着红党，也没在枕头下藏着枪。

sentences.en: We're the 51st state of America.
sentences.zh: 我们是美国的第51个州。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're the 51st state of America.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们是美国的第51个州。

sentences.en: Well, so said the British rock band New Model Army back in 1986, capturing the sense very memorable to those of us who lived through the 80s that America was taking over the world
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是英国摇滚乐队“新模范军”在1986年唱的，它捕捉到了一种对我们这些经历过80年代的人来说非常深刻的感觉，那就是美国正在接管世界，

sentences.en: and we were all turning into little Americans.
sentences.zh: 而我们都在变成小美国人。

sentences.en: Well, welcome to The Rest is History with me, Dominic Sambrick, and my own little American, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史的余味》，我是多米尼克·桑布里克，还有我自己的小美国人，汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: Yeehaw!
sentences.zh: 耶哈！

sentences.en: Hey, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 嘿，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: So, Tom, are you an American-a-phile or American-a-phobe, would you say?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你会说你是“亲美派”还是“恐美派”？

sentences.en: Like everybody, I'm both.
sentences.zh: 和大家一样，我两者都是。

sentences.en: I love America.
sentences.zh: 我爱美国。

sentences.en: Of course, everyone loves America, American culture, but there are times where I feel slightly resentful about how much I love it.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个人都爱美国，爱美国文化，但有时我会对自己如此热爱它感到有点愤恨。

sentences.en: I guess that's a hard frame.
sentences.zh: 我想这是一个很难界定的框架。

sentences.en: I was about to say that's a very British thing, but of course the French, I mean, the French are both, I always think the French are both the biggest American-a-philes
sentences.zh: 我本来想说这是一种非常英国式的想法，但当然法国人也一样，我是说，我一直认为法国人既是最大的“亲美派”，

sentences.en: and the biggest American-a-phobes, so they're the people who go on about Anglo-Saxon culture and all this, but they're also the world's biggest McDonald's consumers.
sentences.zh: 也是最大的“恐美派”。他们总是谈论盎格鲁-撒克逊文化什么的，但他们同时也是世界上麦当劳消费量最大的群体。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess for the French, I mean, in the word Anglo-Saxon, for the French, they bundle Britain in with America.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我想对于法国人来说，在“盎格鲁-撒克逊”这个词里，他们把英国和美国捆绑在一起了。

sentences.en: They do, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们确实是这样，不是吗？

sentences.en: To a degree, so it's Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上是这样，所以就是“盎格鲁-撒克逊人”。

sentences.en: Whereas for us, there's the kind of nagging sense that, you know, we began it and now they've taken over.
sentences.zh: 而对我们来说，有一种挥之不去的念头，你知道，是我们开启了这一切，现在他们却接管了。

sentences.en: It's a bit like us with sport.
sentences.zh: 这有点像我们在体育运动上的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, we invent the sports and then everyone comes and beats us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们发明了这些运动，然后每个人都跑来打败我们。

sentences.en: And slight feeling like that, I think, with America.
sentences.zh: 我想，对美国也有这种微妙的感觉。

sentences.en: It's the slightly staid older brother with the much cooler younger brother, isn't it, I always think.
sentences.zh: 我总觉得，这就像是那个有点古板的哥哥，看着那个酷得多的弟弟，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of course, not something you'll be familiar with, Tom.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对你来说可能不太熟悉，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah, that is very much where I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错，我确实深有同感。

sentences.en: That's where I am too, so.
sentences.zh: 我也是这种感觉。

sentences.en: Okay, so, Americanisation.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么，美国化。

sentences.en: Do you know where the word Americanisation comes from?
sentences.zh: 你知道“美国化”这个词是从哪儿来的吗？

sentences.en: I hope you don't, because I want to tell you.
sentences.zh: 我希望你不知道，因为我想告诉你。

sentences.en: I don't, Dominic, and I'm not interested, so let's move right on.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，多米尼克，而且我也不感兴趣，所以我们直接跳过吧。

sentences.en: Then go on.
sentences.zh: 那就继续吧。

sentences.en: You've obviously been saving it up, bless you.
sentences.zh: 你显然憋了很久了，真是难为你了。

sentences.en: I have, I have.
sentences.zh: 确实，确实。

sentences.en: So, there's a book published in 1902 called The Americanisation of the World by the British newspaper editor W.T.
sentences.zh: 所以，1902年有一本书出版，叫《世界的美国化》，作者是英国报纸编辑W.T.

sentences.en: Stead.
sentences.zh: 斯特德。

sentences.en: And he basically said the United States is going to replace the British Empire
sentences.zh: 他基本上说美国将取代大英帝国，

sentences.en: and, you know, we're all going to end up speaking American and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们最终都会说美式英语，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And, of course, he was right, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 当然，他说对了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we have become Americanised.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们确实已经被美国化了。

sentences.en: I mean, you and I are both of that generation that I think our parents would have looked at us and said,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你和我都是那一代人，我想我们的父母看着我们会说，

sentences.en: or you're using a lot of American slang, you know, you wear American clothes, you watch American TV, too much American TV, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 或者说你用了太多的美国俚语，你知道，你穿美国衣服，看美国电视，看太多的美国电视，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And we have, to some extent, grown up as little Americans, or at least people in the shadow of America, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们确实是作为小美国人长大的，或者至少是生活在美国的阴影下，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, because we grew up in the 80s when we were the kind of unsinkable aircraft carrier for America.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我们是在80年代长大的，那时我们就像是美国那艘“永不沉没的航空母舰”。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we were airstrip one.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们就是“一号机场”。

sentences.en: So I think that, you know, after the Second World War, through the Cold War, American power, military power, economic power, the cultural power was a kind of crucial –
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，二战之后，通过冷战，美国的军事力量、经济力量，文化力量是一种关键的——

sentences.en: I mean, it was both a part of Americanisation, but it was also served to disguise the hardness of American power.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这既是美国化的一部分，也起到了掩盖美国强权冷酷一面的作用。

sentences.en: If you were kind of into jeans and coke and American music, then you might be slightly less worried about the large number of American planes,
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢牛仔裤、可乐和美国音乐，那么你可能就不会那么担心美国在你的国家拥有大量飞机，

sentences.en: you know, sovereign territory on your own country, or the economic power that the dollar exercises, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在你的国土上有主权领地，或者美元所行使的经济权力，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I think that that's – I mean, that's been kind of a feature of the ambivalences towards America, certainly since the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是——我是说，这一直是人们对美国矛盾心理的一个特征，当然是从二战以来。

sentences.en: But actually, I'm interested, though.
sentences.zh: 但其实，我很好奇。

sentences.en: So the word Americanisation dates back to the beginning of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 所以“美国化”这个词可以追溯到20世纪初。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a word that is being applied to something that existed before that, presumably, in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这个词被应用到了一些在此之前，大概在19世纪就已经存在的东西上。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the take-up – so actually, I think most of the traffic was one way, pretty much one way for most of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这种吸收——其实我认为在19世纪的大部分时间里，这种交流基本上是单向的。

sentences.en: So, you know, Dickens goes to America,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，狄更斯去了美国，

sentences.en: British Music Hall goes to America.
sentences.zh: 英国音乐厅文化去了美国。

sentences.en: It does come back a bit, but we are the big daddy, and they are the kind of recipients of our culture.
sentences.zh: 它确实回流了一些，但我们是“老大哥”，他们是我们的文化接受者。

sentences.en: But then I think there's a sense, probably around, you know, 1900 or so, that it's starting to come back the other way, that we are reading American books,
sentences.zh: 但我认为大概在1900年左右，有一种感觉开始反向流动了，我们开始读美国书，

sentences.en: we are becoming familiar with cowboys and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们开始熟悉牛仔等等。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Buffalo Bill.
sentences.zh: 是的，比如布法罗·比尔。

sentences.en: Buffalo Bill and his Wild West show coming round, and huge success.
sentences.zh: 布法罗·比尔和他的“狂野西部”表演巡回演出，取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: And also American heiresses coming over.
sentences.zh: 还有美国女继承人来到英国。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And I know that because that's in Downton Abbey.
sentences.zh: 我知道这一点，因为《唐顿庄园》里有演。

sentences.en: So it must be true.
sentences.zh: 所以那一定是真的。

sentences.en: And so here's a funny thing for you.
sentences.zh: 这里有一件有趣的事。

sentences.en: Eliot, who's from Missouri,
sentences.zh: 艾略特，他来自密苏里州，

sentences.en: is in Oxford, and he spoke in a debate at the Oxford Union, 1914, so before the First World War, about the Americanisation of Oxford.
sentences.zh: 当时在牛津大学，他在1914年牛津辩论社的一场辩论中发言，那是在一战之前，关于牛津的美国化问题。

sentences.en: And what was he saying?
sentences.zh: 他当时说了什么？

sentences.en: He said he was speaking for it.
sentences.zh: 他说他支持美国化。

sentences.en: You know, the motion was, you know, this house deplores the Americanisation of Oxford.
sentences.zh: 你知道，辩题是“本院谴责牛津的美国化”。

sentences.en: T.S.
sentences.zh: T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot was speaking for it, and he said, we see ourselves as cultural missionaries taking the gospel of America out to the world.
sentences.zh: 艾略特当时支持这一动议，他说，我们视自己为文化传教士，将美国的福音带向世界。

sentences.en: I mean, he said it in a teasing way.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他当时是用一种调侃的方式说的。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine T.S.
sentences.zh: 很难想象T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot being that funny, actually.
sentences.zh: 艾略特竟然那么幽默。

sentences.en: Hey, guys.
sentences.zh: 嘿，伙计们。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a brilliant T.S.
sentences.zh: 那真是精彩的T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot impersonation, Tom.
sentences.zh: 艾略特模仿秀，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, worth the entrance price to the podcast alone, just to hear you do your...
sentences.zh: 我是说，光是听你表演这一段，就值回播客的门票钱了……

sentences.en: My famous T.S.
sentences.zh: 我那著名的T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot.
sentences.zh: 艾略特。

sentences.en: April is the cruelest month.
sentences.zh: 四月是最残忍的月份。

sentences.en: Way to go, guys.
sentences.zh: 干得好，伙计们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But what was he thinking?
sentences.zh: 但他当时在想什么？

sentences.en: Say, what was he thinking that Oxford...
sentences.zh: 我是说，他觉得牛津……

sentences.en: How was he thinking Oxford had been Americanised?
sentences.zh: 他认为牛津是如何被美国化的？

sentences.en: Clothes, music, you know, expressions.
sentences.zh: 服装、音乐，你知道，表达方式。

sentences.en: So, I suspect P.G.
sentences.zh: 所以，我怀疑P.G.

sentences.en: Woodhouse's early books have a lot of the mixture of kind of upper-class slang and kind of American slang as well.
sentences.zh: 伍德豪斯早期的书里有很多上流社会俚语和美式俚语的混合。

sentences.en: That's one of P.G.
sentences.zh: 那是P.G.

sentences.en: Woodhouse's big things.
sentences.zh: 伍德豪斯的一大特色。

sentences.en: And then I think, I think, if I'm going to pick one moment that I think marks Americanisation, it's 1927, it's The Jazz Singer.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，如果我要选一个标志着美国化的时刻，那就是1927年的《爵士歌王》。

sentences.en: Because that's the first time, the Al Jolson film, that people actually, large numbers of people, millions of people, are hearing American accents.
sentences.zh: 因为那是阿尔·乔尔森的电影，第一次有大量的人，数以百万计的人，听到了美国口音。

sentences.en: And it's from that point, in the 20s and 30s, that you have...
sentences.zh: 从那时起，在20和30年代，你就有了……

sentences.en: I mean, you have people discussing this in Parliament about the fact that English kids are using American slang, that they are...
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们在议会里讨论这个问题，关于英国孩子使用美国俚语，关于他们……

sentences.en: or they're modelling themselves on movie stars.
sentences.zh: 或者他们以电影明星为榜样。

sentences.en: And the first British...
sentences.zh: 而第一部英国……

sentences.en: The first British film with sound was done by Hitchcock, I think.
sentences.zh: 第一部有声英国电影是希区柯克拍的，我想。

sentences.en: And the way they marketed it, they said, you can hear English as it should be spoken.
sentences.zh: 他们营销的方式是说，你可以听到“应有的英语发音”。

sentences.en: So instead of listening to all this kind of American stuff...
sentences.zh: 所以不用去听那些乱七八糟的美国玩意儿……

sentences.en: A timeless marketing phrase.
sentences.zh: 一个永恒的营销口号。

sentences.en: Well, that's why I choose a film.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我选择电影的原因。

sentences.en: Based on the quality of the spoken English.
sentences.zh: 基于口语英语的质量。

sentences.en: So I think from the 20s onwards, I mean, it's no coincidence that comes in the aftermath of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为从20年代开始，我是说，这并非巧合，它发生在一战之后。

sentences.en: And I think from the 20s onwards, you have this persistent anxiety,
sentences.zh: 我认为从20年代开始，你就有了这种持续的焦虑，

sentences.en: specifically in Britain.
sentences.zh: 特别是在英国。

sentences.en: I mean, there are different kinds of anxiety elsewhere, but I think we have a very particular anxiety that we have been infiltrated, I guess, by American-ness.
sentences.zh: 我是说，其他地方有不同种类的焦虑，但我认为我们有一种非常特殊的焦虑，那就是我们已经被美国性渗透了。

sentences.en: And you have that now, when the arguments about the culture wars and so on, that we're actually...
sentences.zh: 现在也是这样，当谈到文化战争等等时，我们实际上……

sentences.en: We've just imported unthinkingly these American ideas and we're arguing about them and they don't apply to us.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不假思索地引进了这些美国思想，然后为此争论不休，而它们根本不适用于我们。

sentences.en: I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我想这是真的。

sentences.en: But I think that it's interesting, you know, in terms of the culture wars, which I think is actually the way that America is being most influential on us at the moment.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这很有趣，你知道，就文化战争而言，我认为这实际上是目前美国对我们影响最大的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd agree with that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意这一点。

sentences.en: What's interesting is that that, again, is a kind of flip from when we were growing up, when really it was the right that was very pro-American.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这又和我们成长时期的情况完全相反，那时确实是右翼非常亲美。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: All the debate around, you know, again, going back to US air bases in Britain,
sentences.zh: 所有关于，你知道，回到英国的美国空军基地，

sentences.en: Greenham Common, campaigners, CND.
sentences.zh: 格林汉姆公地，抗议者，核裁军运动。

sentences.en: America was seen as the enemy.
sentences.zh: 美国被视为敌人。

sentences.en: Thatcher was disliked, not just for her own sake, but because she was seen as Reagan's mole.
sentences.zh: 撒切尔夫人不受欢迎，不仅是因为她自己，还因为她被视为里根的“内鬼”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The kind of the explosion of finance with the Big Bang and everything in London was seen as a crisis of Americanization.
sentences.zh: 伦敦金融大爆炸带来的金融业爆发，被视为一场美国化的危机。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so Canary Wharf, you know, had the look of America, skyscrapers and things like that.
sentences.zh: 是的，金丝雀码头，你知道，看起来就像美国，摩天大楼之类的东西。

sentences.en: So the sense that Americanization was a kind of right-wing project, I think that's now flipped because I think that the debates, the passions in Britain at the moment
sentences.zh: 所以那种认为美国化是一个右翼项目的观念，我认为现在已经反转了，因为我认为目前英国的辩论和激情，

sentences.en: are massively coming from America.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上来自美国。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's so good.
sentences.zh: 是的，说得太对了。

sentences.en: So now I think it's the left that's been Americanized.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我认为是左翼被美国化了。

sentences.en: So we were talking about Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才在谈论“盎格鲁-撒克逊人”。

sentences.en: The sense that that is a problematic phrase.
sentences.zh: 那种认为这是一个有问题词汇的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah, even the word problematic.
sentences.zh: 是的，甚至“有问题”这个词本身也是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: But you're no longer supposed to use the word Anglo-Saxon to describe the period between the end of the Roman Empire in Britain and the Norman Conquest because Anglo-Saxon is seen
sentences.zh: 但你不再被允许使用“盎格鲁-撒克逊”这个词来描述英国罗马帝国结束到诺曼征服之间的时期，因为“盎格鲁-撒克逊”被视为

sentences.en: as being an inherently racist, white supremacist phrase.
sentences.zh: 是一个本质上种族主义的、白人至上主义的词汇。

sentences.en: But that's only the case in America.
sentences.zh: 但这只是在美国的情况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've seen that.
sentences.zh: 没错，我见过这种情况。

sentences.en: You've been involved in that argument, haven't you, on Twitter?
sentences.zh: 你参与过那场争论，不是吗，在推特上？

sentences.en: It's infuriating.
sentences.zh: 这太令人气愤了。

sentences.en: It's infuriating because, you know, they say we should use, you know, early medieval England or early English.
sentences.zh: 这令人气愤，因为，你知道，他们说我们应该用“早期中世纪英格兰”或“早期英语”。

sentences.en: But it's the English Defence League.
sentences.zh: 但那是“英国保卫联盟”。

sentences.en: It's not the Anglo-Saxon Defence League.
sentences.zh: 不是“盎格鲁-撒克逊保卫联盟”。

sentences.en: Anglo-Saxon doesn't have that connotations here in Britain.
